hook: SCP-1861 is a strange storm with a submarine attached: when it hits, an old naval vessel surfaces in whatever water is nearby, and its suited crew comes ashore to recruit. The article is tagged as a rewrite and leans on two long interviews rather than a lot of procedure. It relies on atmosphere more than shock, but expect some disturbing imagery in the second half.
whyItMatters: It is a good example of horror built on an ambiguous rescue. The crew insist they are saving people, and the article never lets you settle whether that is true, which keeps the entities more interesting than a plain abductor would be. The First World War submarine, the rain and the diving suits give it a distinct, memorable atmosphere.
thingsToNotice:
The two interviews are set up as a pair: the first is a desperate plea from outside, the second a report from someone who went in, and together they show both sides of the same promise. Notice how the second subject's account of the other side resists clear description, and how the interviewer's flippant tone grates against what he is hearing.

The vessel's captain gets only a few lines, but his vocabulary of an ark and a new world hints at a whole mythology the article chooses not to explain. The closing statement answers the question the second interview keeps circling, and it does so in a single dry paragraph.

related.note: Cited in a footnote for a similar rain-related phenomenon.
Another body of red liquid that sends things out into our world.
